nodes.name: sapmap_models.py
nodes.summary: Core dataclasses for the SAP Landscape Attack Path Mapper: severity enum, findings, credentials, created users, forged tickets, trust relations, SAP nodes, RFC connections, SCC and BTP nodes, and the top-level SAPMAPState session container. Every model is JSON-roundtrippable via to_dict/from_dict.
nodes.languageNotes: Each class follows the same convention: dataclass with @field defaults, __post_init__ for invariants, and symmetric to_dict/from_dict for safe .sapmap JSON persistence with backwards-compatible field migrations.

nodes.name: Severity
nodes.summary: IntEnum (CRITICAL=5 .. INFO=1) reused across findings, RFC risk levels, and report color coding.

nodes.name: Finding
nodes.summary: Single security finding attached to a SAPNode: severity, message, category, remediation, evidence, timestamp.

nodes.name: InstanceInfo
nodes.summary: Metadata for one SAP instance number on a node: ports, kernel, services, dispatcher/gateway/MS endpoints.

nodes.name: Credentials
nodes.summary: Username/password/client tuple captured during discovery or exploitation with quality and source tracking; deduplicated on __post_init__.

nodes.name: CreatedUser
nodes.summary: Tracking record for a user account SAPMAP created during an engagement so cleanup can roll them back at the end.

nodes.name: ForgedTicket
nodes.summary: Forged SAP logon ticket model with issuer, subject, validity window, expiration helpers, and use tracking for trust-chain exploitation.

nodes.name: TrustRelation
nodes.summary: Captured SAP trust relation (RFCTRUST / RFCDES Q=Y) between two SIDs with direction and SNC flags.

nodes.name: SAPNode
nodes.summary: Central node on the attack map: hosts, IPs, instances, OS, kernel, findings, credentials, exploit state, secstore loot, BTP/SCC linkage, plus helper accessors like has_access, is_exploitable, and highest_severity.

nodes.name: RFCConnection
nodes.summary: Edge between two SAPNodes representing an RFC destination: type, target user, trust flag, tested status, SAP_ALL flag, and a derived risk_level.

nodes.name: SCCMapping
nodes.summary: Single virtual-to-internal host mapping configured inside a SAP Cloud Connector.

nodes.name: SCCNode
nodes.summary: SAP Cloud Connector node with version, fingerprint, mapped backends, CVE bucket, pwned state and credential loot.

nodes.name: BTPDestination
nodes.summary: Single BTP destination-service entry: name, URL, authentication, captured credentials, and on-prem flag.

nodes.name: BTPSubaccountNode
nodes.summary: BTP subaccount node holding the destination list, region, and the source token used to enumerate it.

nodes.name: SAPMAPState
nodes.summary: Top-level session container: SAP/SCC/BTP nodes, RFC connection list, trust relations, forged tickets, created users, scan config, RFC test cache. Provides add_node/get_node/find_node_by_host/add_connection and the notify_sap_all_if_elevated promotion hook.

nodes.name: sapmap_report.py
nodes.summary: Engagement report builder: walks an SAPMAPState once and produces both portable Markdown and a self-contained HTML deliverable with executive summary, KPI cards, SVG landscape snapshot, hardening checklist, findings, attack coverage, trust chains, credentials, SCC and BTP sections, and structured remediation.
nodes.languageNotes: Twin renderers share helper builders (_executive_summary, _findings_section, etc.) — each returns a list of Markdown lines, which the HTML renderer then upgrades with KPI cards and an inline SVG landscape map produced by _build_landscape_svg.

nodes.name: _executive_summary
nodes.summary: Builds the top-of-report executive summary: scope, key risks, attack outcome, and headline numbers.

nodes.name: _render_structured_remediation
nodes.summary: Renders the structured remediation block (per finding) as Markdown bullets with priority and effort labels.

nodes.name: _html_render_structured_remediation
nodes.summary: HTML variant of the structured remediation renderer with priority pills and color-coded effort cards.

nodes.name: _build_hardening_html
nodes.summary: Builds the HTML hardening guidance block referenced by the hardening checklist section.

nodes.name: _hardening_checklist_section
nodes.summary: Renders the SAP hardening checklist section comparing observed posture against baseline recommendations.

nodes.name: _findings_section
nodes.summary: Renders all findings grouped by severity with per-node detail rows.

nodes.name: _attack_coverage_section
nodes.summary: Renders the attack-coverage matrix showing which exploit primitives were attempted and their outcome per node.

nodes.name: _trust_chains_section
nodes.summary: Renders enumerated trust chains (RFCTRUST/RFCDES Q=Y pivots) with severity ranking.

nodes.name: _per_system_table
nodes.summary: Renders the per-system summary table (SID, host, IP, OS, kernel, pwned state, finding count).

nodes.name: _credentials_section
nodes.summary: Renders the credentials harvest section listing recovered usernames/hashes/cleartext per node.

nodes.name: _scc_section
nodes.summary: Renders the Cloud Connector section listing discovered SCC nodes with version, CVE bucket, and pwned state.

nodes.name: _capability_section
nodes.summary: Renders the capability matrix per node: dispatcher reachable, gateway reachable, MS reachable, RFC working, SAPXPG reachable.

nodes.name: _btp_section
nodes.summary: Renders the BTP subaccount and destination summary section.

nodes.name: _derive_landscape_recommendations
nodes.summary: Large rule engine that inspects the state and derives concrete, prioritized landscape-wide recommendations (gateway ACLs, MS internal port firewalling, RFC trust pruning, SCC patching, etc.).

nodes.name: _recommendations_section
nodes.summary: Formats the derived recommendation list into a Markdown / HTML section with priority badges.

nodes.name: build_markdown_report
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point: assembles the full engagement report as portable Markdown by composing all section helpers.

nodes.name: _kpi_card
nodes.summary: Builds an HTML KPI card (label, big number, color tint) used in the HTML report header.

nodes.name: _build_landscape_svg
nodes.summary: Renders a self-contained inline SVG snapshot of the discovered SAP landscape — node boxes, RFC edges, trust chains — to embed directly in the HTML report.

nodes.name: build_html_report
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point: assembles the self-contained engagement HTML deliverable with KPI cards, inline SVG landscape, styled sections, and structured remediation.

nodes.name: sapmap_state.py
nodes.summary: Session persistence layer: saves/loads SAPMAPState to/from .sapmap JSON files in states/, maintains an RFC test cache and a created-destination log across sessions, manages the loot directory tree (secstore/hashes/tables/bia), and lists prior saved sessions.
nodes.languageNotes: PROJECT_ROOT is derived from __file__ so moving this module within the source tree does not relocate user state or loot directories.

nodes.name: ensure_loot_dir
nodes.summary: Creates the loot directory tree (secstore, hashes, tables, bia subdirs) on demand.

nodes.name: save_state
nodes.summary: Serializes the SAPMAPState to a .sapmap JSON file, writing atomically via a temp file and rename.

nodes.name: load_state
nodes.summary: Loads and deserializes a .sapmap JSON file into a SAPMAPState instance, handling legacy fields and corrupt files gracefully.

nodes.name: _save_rfc_cache
nodes.summary: Persists the RFC test cache to disk to avoid relocking accounts across sessions.

nodes.name: _load_rfc_cache
nodes.summary: Loads the persistent RFC test cache.

nodes.name: load_rfc_cache_into
nodes.summary: Loads the RFC test cache and merges it into the given SAPMAPState instance.

nodes.name: reset_rfc_cache
nodes.summary: Clears the on-disk RFC test cache (used after credentials have been rotated).

nodes.name: save_created_destination
nodes.summary: Appends a record of a created RFC destination to the destinations log for later cleanup.

nodes.name: _load_dest_log
nodes.summary: Loads the created-destination log file.

nodes.name: load_created_destinations_into
nodes.summary: Loads the destinations log and applies its entries to the given SAPMAPState for cleanup tracking.

nodes.name: clear_created_destinations
nodes.summary: Truncates the destinations log once cleanup has succeeded.

nodes.name: auto_save_path
nodes.summary: Returns the path to the auto-save .sapmap file used on graceful shutdown.

nodes.name: list_saved_states
nodes.summary: Returns a list of saved .sapmap files in states/ with timestamps so the GUI can populate its load menu.

nodes.name: sapmap_diff.py
nodes.summary: Computes a structured delta between two SAPMAPState snapshots (added/removed/changed SAP nodes, findings, RFC connections, cloud connectors, trust chains, created users) and renders the diff as Markdown or self-contained HTML matching the engagement-report visual language.
nodes.languageNotes: Three parallel renderers (compute_state_diff plus build_diff_markdown and build_diff_html) all share a small set of identity-key helpers (_conn_key, _finding_key) so a single matching algorithm drives both renderings.

nodes.name: compute_state_diff
nodes.summary: Walks two SAPMAPState instances and produces the canonical delta dictionary used by every diff renderer: added/removed/changed SAP nodes, findings, RFC connections, SCC nodes, and trust chains.

nodes.name: build_diff_markdown
nodes.summary: Renders the diff dict from compute_state_diff as portable Markdown with section tables for changed nodes, findings, and trust chains.

nodes.name: build_diff_html
nodes.summary: Renders a self-contained HTML diff page with KPI delta cards, color-coded changes, and inline CSS matching the engagement report styling.

nodes.name: _node_summary
nodes.summary: Builds a compact dict of the SAPNode fields whose changes are reportable (pwned, is_production, has_critical_finding, credentials count, findings count).

nodes.name: _conn_summary
nodes.summary: Builds the reportable subset of an RFCConnection used for matching and change detection across snapshots.

nodes.name: _changed_node_fields
nodes.summary: Identifies which SAPNode fields differ between two snapshots, returning a list of (field, before, after) tuples.

nodes.name: _changed_scc_fields
nodes.summary: Identifies changed fields on an SCC (Cloud Connector) node such as pwned status, default credential liveness, or version.

nodes.name: _delta_kpi
nodes.summary: Builds an HTML KPI card showing a before/after numeric delta with directional color coding for the diff dashboard.

nodes.name: sapmap_findings.py
nodes.summary: Module-global findings bus that decouples the discovery and exploit modules from the GUI: any code can call emit_finding(severity, node, msg) and registered listeners receive the dict in real time, with a 60-second dedupe window and 500-entry ring buffer.
nodes.languageNotes: Module-level state (lock, listeners list, ring buffer) rather than a class so any subsystem can import and emit without owning a singleton handle.

nodes.name: register_listener
nodes.summary: Subscribes a callable to receive every emitted finding; the GUI registers a listener at start-up to push findings into the console and session drawer.

nodes.name: _persist_to_node
nodes.summary: Attaches an emitted finding to the right SAPNode in the live SAPMAPState so the GUI's per-node finding lists stay in sync without explicit callbacks.

nodes.name: emit_finding
nodes.summary: Primary publisher: deduplicates within a 60-second window, persists to the node if a state is attached, appends to the ring buffer, and fans out to all listeners — used by every scanner and exploit module to surface findings.

nodes.name: get_since
nodes.summary: Returns findings emitted after a given monotonic id, used by the GUI poll loop to fetch incremental updates.

nodes.name: snapshot
nodes.summary: Returns the current findings ring buffer as a serializable list for inclusion in the state save.

nodes.name: load_snapshot
nodes.summary: Restores the findings ring buffer from a previously serialized snapshot when reloading a saved session.

nodes.name: sapmap_gui.py
nodes.summary: Bottle HTTP backend exposing 60+ REST routes for the SAPMAP single-page app: discovery, RFC operations, exploitation, payload generation, SCC enumeration, console streaming, and session save/load. All long-running tasks run in background threads while the JS frontend polls for state updates.
nodes.languageNotes: Single 9.6k-line create_app factory builds the entire Bottle app — routes capture closure state over the SAPMAPState singleton, the OutputCapture stdout sink, and shell-session bookkeeping.

nodes.name: OutputCapture
nodes.summary: stdout/stderr tee that mirrors print() output into the GUI console buffer so scanner and exploit logs reach the frontend without each module knowing about Bottle.

nodes.name: ShellSession
nodes.summary: Per-target reverse/bind shell session: listener socket, connector reader thread, and bidirectional buffer that the frontend reads via a poll endpoint and writes to via a send endpoint.

nodes.name: SAPMAPApi
nodes.summary: pywebview JavaScript bridge: methods exposed to the embedded browser to start/stop scans and pull a serializable view of the SAPMAPState.

nodes.name: create_app
nodes.summary: Builds and returns the Bottle application with all REST endpoints (discovery, RFC tables, exploitation, SCC, CVE-2025-31324, BTP, secstore extraction, payload generation, session management) wired against a single SAPMAPState instance.

nodes.name: _derive_sid
nodes.summary: Derives a 3-character SAP SID from an RFC destination name or hostname using SAP naming conventions, with fallbacks for non-standard hosts.

nodes.name: _resolve_host
nodes.summary: Resolves a hostname to an IP via DNS with a short timeout, used to canonicalise nodes added by RFC destination crawls.

nodes.name: _console_push_finding
nodes.summary: Listener registered with sapmap_findings.register_listener — formats each finding with severity color tags and pushes it into the console ring buffer.

nodes.name: _signal_all_betrusted_stops
nodes.summary: Sets every registered Message-Server betrusted stop event so an in-flight CVE-2020-6207 chain can be cancelled cleanly from the GUI.

nodes.name: _bg
nodes.summary: Spawns a daemon thread that runs a long task and registers it under a task-id for GUI polling and cancellation.

nodes.name: _set_wd_port_protocol
nodes.summary: Normalises the WebDispatcher port/protocol fields on a node based on whether HTTPS or HTTP was observed during probing.

nodes.name: _enrich_wd_backends_from_admin_table
nodes.summary: Parses a WebDispatcher /sap/wdisp/admin backend table page and creates or updates downstream SAPNodes for every backend listed, including ICM and J2EE entries.

nodes.name: _detect_local_ip
nodes.summary: Detects the operator's outbound IP via a UDP-connect probe, used to populate reverse-shell and CVE-2020-6207 callback addresses.

nodes.name: _enumerate_windows_drives
nodes.summary: Enumerates mounted drive letters on a compromised Windows host via dir output parsing so SCC and SAP-instance root discovery can sweep every volume.

nodes.name: _expand_scc_roots_across_drives
nodes.summary: Returns the cartesian product of SCC install-root candidates across every discovered drive letter on a Windows target.

nodes.name: _win_multistep_payload
nodes.summary: Builds a chunked Windows command payload that decodes and runs a base64 PowerShell shellcode in multiple steps to bypass command-length limits in Gateway and dpmon execution channels.

nodes.name: _detect_is_windows
nodes.summary: Probes a target via SAPXPG/dpmon command execution to determine whether it is running Windows or a Unix variant.

nodes.name: _detect_python_cmd
nodes.summary: Probes the target for a usable python or python3 binary so reverse-shell payloads can pick the available interpreter.

nodes.name: _perl_reverse_shell
nodes.summary: Generates a one-line Perl reverse-shell payload that connects back to the operator and execs /bin/sh.

nodes.name: _perl_bind_shell
nodes.summary: Generates a Perl bind-shell payload that listens on a port and execs /bin/sh on connection.

nodes.name: _generate_payload
nodes.summary: Picks the best reverse-shell payload (python, perl, bash, PowerShell) based on detected OS and available interpreters and returns the command string.

nodes.name: _generate_bind_payload
nodes.summary: Picks the best bind-shell payload variant for the target OS and returns the listener command and the connect-back instructions for the operator.

nodes.name: _build_linuxlpe_shell_dispatch
nodes.summary: Assembles the Linux LPE shell-dispatch command sequence wrapping a chosen privilege-escalation primitive (sapxpg, suid, kernel) with stage-by-stage logging.

nodes.name: sapmap_html.py
nodes.summary: Single self-contained 11k-line HTML/CSS/JavaScript bundle for the SAPMAP frontend: interactive SVG landscape map with pan/zoom/drag, RFC connection rendering, right-click context menus, credential dialogs, real-time console, and status bar. Exposed via the single get_html() function.
nodes.languageNotes: Entire SPA is embedded as a Python triple-quoted string constant so the GUI has zero external static-file dependencies and can serve the whole UI from one route.

nodes.name: get_html
nodes.summary: Returns the complete single-page-app HTML string for the SAPMAP GUI.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package initializer that appends every modules subpackage directory to sys.path so callers can use flat imports (e.g., `from sapmap_models import ...`) regardless of caller location.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel using sys.path manipulation rather than re-exports — supports the project-wide flat-import convention.

nodes.name: sapmap.py
nodes.summary: Main CLI entry point for SAPMAP — parses arguments, launches the Bottle HTTP server, manages the pywebview GUI window (with GTK/macOS patches), and orchestrates state loading, scripted scenarios, and CLI-only scans.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses lazy imports for pywebview/GTK and threading.Thread for background Bottle server; includes a runtime monkey-patch for pywebview's evaluate_javascript signature mismatch on GTK.

nodes.name: conftest.py
nodes.summary: Pytest configuration that registers every modules subpackage directory on sys.path, mirroring the production package initializer so tests can use flat imports.

nodes.name: capture_real_ticket.py
nodes.summary: Research utility that logs into a real SAP J2EE NetWeaver instance via HTTPS form authentication, captures the MYSAPSSO2 logon ticket, decodes/parses it, and compares against a forged ticket to validate the project's ticket-forging implementation.

nodes.name: compare_with_sap_ticket.py
nodes.summary: Diagnostic tool that reads an SAP-issued MYSAPSSO2 ticket via the Gateway SAPXPG channel and compares its structure (including PKCS#7 BER fields) against a locally forged ticket to validate forging fidelity.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes a hand-rolled BER tag-length parser and PKCS#7 SignedData walker — used to compare authentic SAP tickets against the project's forger output.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Argument-parsing and startup orchestrator: builds the SAPMAPApi state, optionally loads a prior session, starts the Bottle HTTP server thread, runs scripted scenarios, and either launches pywebview or opens the system browser.

nodes.name: _patch_pywebview_gtk
nodes.summary: Monkey-patches WebKit2.WebView.run_javascript and related GTK pywebview internals so newer WebKit2 versions (with run_javascript_finish signature changes) keep working with pywebview's JS evaluation.
nodes.languageNotes: Targets a known regression in pywebview's GTK backend against newer WebKit2 builds.

nodes.name: _try_pywebview
nodes.summary: Attempts to launch the GUI inside a pywebview window with platform-specific icon and process-name configuration (GTK GLib for Linux, AppKit NSImage for macOS); returns False to signal the caller should fall back to the system browser.

nodes.name: _cli_scan
nodes.summary: Headless CLI scan: parses target CIDR/host list, calls discover_systems, registers found nodes in state, prints a summary table, and auto-saves the resulting .sapmap session file.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Drives the end-to-end ticket capture flow: opens an HTTPS session, scrapes hidden form fields, submits credentials, parses the resulting Set-Cookie MYSAPSSO2 ticket, then forges an equivalent ticket locally and prints a field-by-field comparison.

nodes.name: _summarize_pkcs7
nodes.summary: Walks a PKCS#7 SignedData DER blob using a hand-rolled BER tag-length reader and prints content-type OIDs, digest algorithms, signer info, and signature fields for forensic comparison between SAP-issued and locally forged tickets.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements just enough BER parsing to navigate the PKCS#7 structure without pulling in cryptography/pyasn1 dependencies.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Reads an authentic MYSAPSSO2 ticket from disk on the target SAP host via Gateway SAPXPG-driven file read, parses it, then forges a local equivalent using the project's signing-key extraction and ticket-forge helpers and prints a field-level diff.

nodes.name: sap_betrusted_chain.py
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the Message Server betrusted + Gateway 10KBLAZE exploit chain: registers a fake internal application server via the MS internal port, then leverages the resulting trust to invoke SAPXPG OS commands without authentication.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses background threads with stop_event coordination to keep the MS betrusted hijack alive while a parallel Gateway exploit runs.

nodes.name: _get_local_ip_towards
nodes.summary: Resolves the local outbound IP that would be used to reach a target host by opening a UDP socket and reading the chosen source address.

nodes.name: try_betrusted_chain
nodes.summary: Probes a node for the betrusted+Gateway chain: spawns a background MS betrusted hijack thread, polls for completion, then verifies that the gateway has become exploitable from the new trusted identity.

nodes.name: create_user_betrusted_chain
nodes.summary: Drives the betrusted chain to create the persistent SAPMAP user: keeps the MS betrusted thread alive while invoking the standard Gateway exploit user-creation routine.

nodes.name: sap_db_sql_writers.py
nodes.summary: Multi-database SQL execution layer for the Gateway 10KBLAZE primitive: emits per-DB (Oracle, MSSQL, HANA, MaxDB, DB2) OS command sequences that pipe SQL into the local DB client through SAPXPG.
nodes.languageNotes: Per-database writers encode SQL via Windows cmd caret-escaping or shell-quoted heredocs to survive transit through the Gateway SAPXPG OS-exec primitive.

nodes.name: _cmd_caret_escape
nodes.summary: Escapes shell metacharacters in a string for safe inclusion in Windows cmd.exe echo statements written through the SAPXPG channel.

nodes.name: _oracle_write_and_exec_win
nodes.summary: Writes an Oracle SQL script to disk via chunked Windows echo commands through Gateway SAPXPG, then invokes sqlplus to execute it as the database owner.

nodes.name: _mssql_write_and_exec_win
nodes.summary: Writes a T-SQL script via Windows echo chunks through Gateway SAPXPG, then runs sqlcmd against the local MSSQL instance to create the SAPMAP user.

nodes.name: _hana_write_and_exec
nodes.summary: Executes SAP HANA SQL via hdbsql through the Gateway SAPXPG channel, supporting both Windows and Linux hosts with the appropriate quoting style.

nodes.name: _maxdb_write_and_exec
nodes.summary: Runs MaxDB/liveCache SQL via the dbmcli/sqlcli client through Gateway SAPXPG, choosing the correct binary and quoting per OS.

nodes.name: _execute_sql_via_gateway
nodes.summary: Top-level dispatcher that normalizes the DB type, picks the right per-database writer, and runs the resulting OS command through a fresh Gateway connection.

nodes.name: sapmap_exploit.py
nodes.summary: Central exploitation orchestrator: probes Gateway vulnerability, runs 10KBLAZE OS execution, forges/uses SAP logon tickets, deploys CVE-2025-31324 webshells, creates SAPMAP users across ABAP and Java stacks, and propagates the foothold across the RFC trust graph.
nodes.languageNotes: 4867-line god-module that glues together every exploit primitive (10KBLAZE, betrusted, CVE-2025-31324, dpmon SAP*, Java telnet/CTC) behind a uniform per-node execution interface.

nodes.name: _gw_connect
nodes.summary: Opens a NI/SAProuter-aware TCP socket to a Gateway port with a configurable timeout, returning the connected socket for further protocol framing.

nodes.name: _find_gw_port
nodes.summary: Picks the most likely Gateway port for a node based on instance number and previously discovered open-port hints.

nodes.name: _find_gw_ports_all
nodes.summary: Enumerates all plausible Gateway ports for a node (33XX, 48XX, secondary instances) so probes can fan out across every candidate.

nodes.name: check_gw_vulnerable
nodes.summary: Probes a node's Gateway ports for the 10KBLAZE SAPXPG misconfiguration and records the verdict on the node for later use by the user-creation routines.

nodes.name: _probe_gw_port_for_xpg
nodes.summary: Executes the four-phase Gateway NI handshake against a single port to determine whether SAPXPG registration succeeds without authentication.

nodes.name: execute_gw_command
nodes.summary: Executes an arbitrary OS command on a target through the Gateway SAPXPG primitive, returning captured stdout/stderr and rotating across candidate ports on failure.

nodes.name: _make_node_gw_exec_fn
nodes.summary: Returns a closure that runs OS commands on a given node via the Gateway primitive, used as a uniform exec adapter for downstream helpers like dpmon and SecStore.

nodes.name: extract_and_forge_ticket
nodes.summary: Steals SAP logon ticket signing material from the target's PSE/SecStore and forges an SSO2 ticket for any user, optionally restricting validity and recipient SID.

nodes.name: create_user_via_ticket
nodes.summary: Uses a forged SAP logon ticket to authenticate to ICF/SOAP endpoints and create the SAPMAP user with SAP_ALL on the target ABAP node.

nodes.name: execute_cve_2025_31324_command
nodes.summary: Runs a single OS command on the target via the CVE-2025-31324 VisualComposer JSP webshell that was previously dropped.

nodes.name: execute_cve_2025_31324_via_shell
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that lazily drops the CVE-2025-31324 JSP webshell if needed and then proxies a command through it.

nodes.name: _cve_31324_command_write_shell
nodes.summary: Builds the chunked-base64 file-write payload that delivers the JSP webshell through the CVE-2025-31324 unauthenticated upload endpoint.

nodes.name: drop_cve_2025_31324_shell
nodes.summary: Drops and verifies the CVE-2025-31324 JSP webshell on the target VisualComposer endpoint, recording the URL on the node.

nodes.name: _telnet_deploy_available
nodes.summary: Decides whether the Java telnet administration channel is reachable and credentialed for JSP deployment on this node.

nodes.name: _ctc_deploy_available
nodes.summary: Checks whether the SAP CTC (Configuration Wizard) deploy interface is reachable and credentialed on this Java node.

nodes.name: _deploy_jsp_via_ctc
nodes.summary: Uploads a JSP payload to a Java AS through the CTC admin endpoint using the resolved Java administrator credentials.

nodes.name: _deploy_jsp_via_telnet
nodes.summary: Deploys a JSP file to the Java AS by scripting the SAP Java telnet admin shell across the candidate endpoint set.

nodes.name: create_user_java
nodes.summary: Creates an Administrators-group user on the Java stack by trying telnet, CTC, JSP-shell, and CVE-2025-31324 webshell channels in priority order.

nodes.name: _find_node_by_host_flex
nodes.summary: Looks up an existing SAPNode in the state by matching host, IP, or short hostname with optional SID exclusion.

nodes.name: _probe_and_add_host
nodes.summary: Probes a newly discovered host (e.g. trust target) for SAP services and registers a matching SAPNode in the state if found.

nodes.name: _build_java_os_exec
nodes.summary: Constructs a callable that runs OS commands on the Java node via whichever webshell/telnet channel is currently available.

nodes.name: offline_decrypt_secstore
nodes.summary: Pulls the ABAP SecStore key+data and decrypts it offline through RSECTAB/RSECCipher fallbacks, surfacing rows that resist all methods.

nodes.name: run_os_command
nodes.summary: Generic per-node OS command runner that picks the highest-confidence channel (Gateway, CVE-2025-31324, Java) registered on the node.

nodes.name: create_user_gw_exploit
nodes.summary: End-to-end SAPMAP user creation through the 10KBLAZE Gateway primitive: detects DB type, generates SQL, executes via SAPXPG, then verifies the credential works over RFC.

nodes.name: create_user_via_dpmon_sap_star
nodes.summary: Activates the virtual SAP* account via dpmon (SAP Note 3303172) over an existing OS-exec channel and uses it to create the SAPMAP user.

nodes.name: create_user_via_tcpip
nodes.summary: Hops to a downstream node via a discovered TCP/IP RFC destination and creates the SAPMAP user using the inherited trust.

nodes.name: _deploy_jsp_via_gw
nodes.summary: Stages a JSP webshell on a Java host by writing the file via Gateway SAPXPG OS commands when telnet/CTC paths are unavailable.

nodes.name: _check_sapmap_user_reusable
nodes.summary: Tests whether the standard SAPMAP credentials already log in on a target node, letting the orchestrator skip re-exploitation when persistence is intact.

nodes.name: create_user_via_credentials
nodes.summary: Creates the SAPMAP user on a node where authenticated RFC credentials are already known, bypassing the unauthenticated exploit chain.

nodes.name: _try_secstore_direct_login
nodes.summary: Replays SecStore-extracted credentials directly against a destination's target to confirm cleartext passwords still work for lateral movement.

nodes.name: propagate_from_node
nodes.summary: Walks the RFC trust graph from a foothold node and propagates the SAPMAP user across every reachable destination, recording per-edge results.

nodes.name: propagate_all
nodes.summary: Fan-out wrapper that calls propagate_from_node on every owned entry node up to a configured depth.

nodes.name: _post_exploit_enrichment
nodes.summary: Runs lightweight post-exploit enrichment (system type detection, LPE check, banner refresh) after a successful user creation.

nodes.name: _detect_and_set_system_type
nodes.summary: Classifies a node as ABAP, Java, or dual-stack based on probes and proven exploit paths and stores the verdict on the SAPNode.

nodes.name: sapmap_efspotato.py
nodes.summary: Windows LPE module that escalates to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM by coercing lsass.exe via MS-EFSRPC named-pipe authentication, complementing GodPotato on hardened hosts where DCOM unmarshalling yields only Identification-level tokens.

nodes.name: run_as_system
nodes.summary: Main exploit driver — uploads the GodPotato exe, verifies SHA-256, triggers DCOM unmarshalling coercion of RPCSS, and runs an operator-supplied command as SYSTEM, returning certutil-decoded output.

nodes.name: check_miniplasma

nodes.name: run_as_system

tour.title: What SAPMAP Is
tour.description: Begin with the README to understand the project's premise: "like BloodHound for Active Directory, but for SAP." SAPMAP discovers SAP systems, maps RFC trust between them, fires known exploits (10KBLAZE, MS betrusted, CVE-2025-31324, MYSAPSSO2 forge, Windows LPE), and renders the resulting attack surface as an interactive web map. The DISCLAIMER alongside is non-negotiable context: this is a research/red-team tool that requires written authorization before use.

tour.title: The Entry Point — What `python3 sapmap.py` Actually Does
tour.description: `sapmap.py` is the single entry the user runs. It parses CLI flags, optionally registers the SAP NW RFC SDK path, then either launches a Bottle HTTP server with a pywebview GUI window, runs a scripted scenario, or executes a headless CLI scan. Note the inbound edges from many config and doc files: every demo playbook and the README all reference this file — it really is the front door. `requirements.txt` lists the minimal pinned deps (bottle, requests, urllib3, pycryptodome) and the optional lazy extras (pywebview, pyyaml, pyjks, SAPology) that are only imported when a specific feature is invoked.
tour.languageLesson: Python's lazy-import idiom: top-level imports stay minimal, and heavy/optional dependencies are imported *inside* the function that needs them. SAPMAP uses this so unauthenticated features work even when the NW RFC SDK, pyrfc, pyjks, etc. are not installed — ImportErrors surface at use time, not startup.

tour.title: The Flat-Import Trick — How `modules/*` Glues Together
tour.description: Before any module can `from sapmap_models import ...`, somebody has to make that work. `modules/__init__.py` walks every subpackage directory and appends it to `sys.path` at import time. This is the *only* import the entry point directly makes, which is why most cross-module dependencies don't show up as edges in the graph — they resolve through the flat namespace created here. `tests/conftest.py` mirrors the same trick so pytest can use identical import paths.
tour.languageLesson: Mutating `sys.path` at package init is a deliberate ergonomics tradeoff: it lets every file write short flat imports regardless of nesting depth, at the cost of opaque dependency relationships and harder static analysis. SAPMAP accepts that tradeoff so it can keep the module tree shallow and the imports readable.

tour.title: The Domain Model — What SAPMAP Is Mapping
tour.description: Every node, edge, and finding the tool collects is a dataclass defined here. `SAPNode`, `RFCConnection`, `Credentials`, `TrustRelation`, `Finding`, `SCCNode`, `BTPDestination`, and the top-level `SAPMAPState` container give the project its vocabulary. Each model is JSON-roundtrippable via `to_dict`/`from_dict`, which is the contract that makes `.sapmap` session files plain inspectable JSON. Understand these dataclasses and you understand what every later step is producing.

tour.title: Session State, Persistence, and the Findings Bus
tour.description: `sapmap_state.py` is the persistence layer — it saves and loads `.sapmap` JSON files in `states/`, maintains an RFC test cache, and provisions the `loot/` directory tree (secstore, hashes, tables, bia) where extracted secrets land. `sapmap_findings.py` is a module-global pub/sub bus that decouples discovery and exploit code from the GUI: anything can `emit_finding(severity, node, msg)` and registered listeners receive a structured dict in real time, with a 60-second dedupe window and a 500-entry ring buffer. This is the loose-coupling backbone that lets background threads stream events to the SVG map without callbacks.

tour.title: The Web GUI — Bottle Server + Single-File Frontend
tour.description: The user-visible map is built from two files. `sapmap_gui.py` is a Bottle HTTP backend exposing 60+ REST routes for discovery, RFC operations, exploitation, payload generation, SCC enumeration, and session save/load; every long-running operation runs in a background thread while the frontend polls for state updates. `sapmap_html.py` is an 11k-line self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript bundle (no external JS deps) returning the entire single-page app from one `get_html()` function — interactive SVG landscape with pan/zoom/drag, RFC connection rendering, right-click menus, and a real-time console. Together they replace what BloodHound's neo4j-backed UI does, but with zero third-party runtime dependencies.
tour.languageLesson: Polling vs. callbacks: SAPMAP's frontend polls REST endpoints for state instead of using WebSockets or server-sent events. This is a deliberate simplicity choice — Bottle stays a plain WSGI app, background threads never have to know about clients, and the JS side just refreshes the SVG when a poll returns new data.

tour.title: Discovery — Finding SAP Systems on the Wire
tour.description: Discovery is where the landscape gets populated. `sapmap_scanner.py` runs in two modes: fast (dispatcher 32XX + gateway 33XX ports only) and deep (via SAPology integration). For every reachable system it materializes a `SAPNode` (from Step 4) into the `SAPMAPState`. `sap_default_creds.py` then probes each system with 16 well-known credential pairs via the DIAG protocol, sequentially to minimize lockout risk. Every hit emits a finding (Step 5's bus) that the GUI map renders as a red badge on the node.

tour.title: RFC Trust Mapping — How the Edges Get Drawn
tour.description: This is the BloodHound analogy made literal. `sapmap_rfc.py` performs authenticated RFC operations against each discovered ABAP system: BAPI calls, `RFC_READ_TABLE` against RFCDES/RFCSYSACL, destination management, user creation. By reading the RFC destinations table from one system, SAPMAP learns which other systems it trusts — those become `RFCConnection` and `TrustRelation` edges between the `SAPNode`s on the map. The trust graph that emerges is what later powers the attack-chain ranking.

tour.title: The Protocol Layer — RFC over the Wire, Through SAProuter
tour.description: Underneath the RFC operations sits a tier of low-level protocol code. `sap_rfc_ctypes.py` is a lazy-loaded ctypes wrapper around the proprietary SAP NW RFC SDK (so the rest of the codebase keeps working when the SDK is absent). `sap_rfc_system_info.py` performs *unauthenticated* probing through three fallback methods (V6 single-packet, V2 error-leak, Chipik-style) to extract SID/kernel/hostname without credentials. `sap_saprouter.py` transparently wraps every scan/RFC/exploit call so traffic can tunnel through a target's SAProuter — this is what lets a single SAPMAP run map an internal landscape from the outside.
tour.languageLesson: ctypes lazy-loading: by importing the SDK only when an authenticated RFC feature is first called, the entire unauthenticated discovery + exploit surface remains usable without installing the proprietary NW RFC SDK. The ImportError becomes a runtime error you can show in the GUI, not a hard startup failure.

tour.title: Unauthenticated Exploitation — 10KBLAZE and Message Server Trust
tour.description: Now the offensive payload modules. `sapmap_exploit.py` is the central orchestrator: it probes Gateway vulnerability, runs the 10KBLAZE chain, deploys CVE-2025-31324 webshells, creates SAPMAP users on ABAP and Java stacks, and propagates the foothold across the trust graph from Step 8. `sap_gw_xpg_standalone.py` is the pure-Python 10KBLAZE Gateway SAPXPG primitive (unauthenticated OS command execution via misconfigured `secinfo`/`reginfo`). `sap_ms_betrusted.py` exploits the Message Server internal port (CVE-2020-6207) to register a fake application server, and `sap_betrusted_chain.py` glues the two together: register-fake-server-then-call-SAPXPG yields unauthenticated RCE on hardened gateways.

tour.title: Modern CVEs and SSO Forgery — CVE-2025-31324 and MYSAPSSO2
tour.description: `sap_cve_2025_31324.py` exploits a recent VisualComposer flaw by chunked-base64-writing a JSP webshell into a Java NetWeaver install, giving you OS-level code on the Java stack. `sap_mysapsso2.py` goes the other direction: it forges MYSAPSSO2 logon tickets (SAP's portal SSO format) so a compromise of one trusted system buys instant authenticated access to every other system that accepts those tickets. Together they extend the 10KBLAZE-era attack surface from Step 10 into 2025-era SAP landscapes.

tour.title: Post-Exploitation — LPE, SecStore Looting, Attack-Chain BFS
tour.description: Once a foothold exists, three things happen. `sapmap_lpe.py` runs decorator-registered privilege-escalation methods — `bapi_profiles_assign` grants SAP_ALL via direct RFC; `webgui_rsbdcos0` injects SQL through the WebGUI to bypass `S_RFC`. `sapmap_secstore.py` decrypts the ABAP RSECTAB SecStore using SAP's proprietary RSECCipher (an 8-round Feistel over 3DES) through a 5-method fallback chain, surfacing cleartext credentials into the `loot/` tree from Step 5. Finally, `sapmap_chain.py` does the BloodHound moment: BFS over the RFC adjacency graph from every entry point, ranking paths by severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) — this is the algorithm that turns the discovered graph into ranked lateral-movement chains.
tour.languageLesson: Decorator-registered method dispatch: `sapmap_lpe.py` uses a Python decorator (e.g. `@lpe_method(...)`) to auto-register escalation techniques into a central registry at import time. Adding a new LPE is just defining a function with the decorator — no central if/elif chain to edit, no plugin manifest. This is the same pattern Flask/pytest use for routes and fixtures.

tour.title: Reporting and Scripted Scenarios — Closing the Loop
tour.description: An engagement isn't done until there's a deliverable. `sapmap_report.py` walks the final `SAPMAPState` and emits both portable Markdown and a self-contained HTML report with KPI cards, an SVG snapshot of the landscape, attack coverage, trust chains, credentials, SCC/BTP sections, and structured remediation. `demo_10kblaze.yaml` shows the other half of automation: a scripted playbook that drives the whole pipeline (MS betrusted IP injection → Gateway SAPXPG user creation → RFC harvesting → SecStore download → business-impact assessment) without ever opening the GUI — exactly the chain you just walked through, expressed as data. Run this file via `python3 sapmap.py --script scripts/demo_10kblaze.yaml` and you've executed the full README story end-to-end.
tour.languageLesson: YAML as a DSL for scenarios: the playbook format is plain YAML mapping step names to module/function calls with kwargs. There's no custom parser — `pyyaml.safe_load` returns a dict, and the scenario runner dispatches each step against the same module functions the GUI calls. Demo files double as integration tests and as reproducible engagement evidence.
